messages:
jessica: Quick question — for docs-only PRs that don't touch config or runtime defaults, do we expect a semver bump?

mike: My take: docs-only shouldn't bump at all. Just a changelog entry under 'docs'.

anh: Agreed in principle but deploybot still enforces a version change for every release PR unless labelled. We should make that label path clearer.

cameron: Current pain: devs forget to add the `release: docs-only` label, deploybot forces a patch increment and CI fails with the releasebot check.

jessica: Right — proposal: Add a `docs-only` label that bypasses releasebot's mandatory bump. Docs that change defaults or behavior (e.g., default timeout) would still require at least a patch.

mike: +1. Can we codify in PR template: "Does this change runtime behavior? yes/no" and auto-suggest label?

anh: We can. Also thinking about edgecases: examples/snippets that update SDK surface (like adding a new example method) — that feels like docs but might imply API surface change.

cameron: If it touches public API signatures or published SDKs -> minor. If it's examples only -> docs-only. We should add a short decision matrix in CONTRIBUTING.md.

deploybot: INFO: current releasebot version 3.4.1 — to opt-out of bump, add label `docs-only` or `chore/no-bump`. Failing check: `releasebot/bump-required`

jessica: Perfect. Next: tagging conventions in releases. Some folks want human-friendly tags like `v1.4.2` vs machine-only `1.4.2+meta`. Thoughts?

mike: I prefer `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` as git tags and keep buildmeta in annotated tag body (not in ref). Keeps CI tooling simpler.

anh: We currently append `+build.<sha>` during automated builds which broke some semver parsers. If we keep annotated message it won't break tools.

cameron: So policy: tag ref = `v1.4.2`, annotated message contains `build-meta: sha=abcdef, ci=prod`. Deploybot reads annotated message for metadata.

jessica: Sounds good. Also want release notes requirement: every release (including docs-only) needs a release-notes snippet. Docs-only can have a single-line item under "Documentation". Releasebot should auto-generate the GitHub release body from PR descriptions when label present.

mike: Can we add a lightweight checklist in PRs: `- [ ] release-notes added (if applicable)`, and have a lint that fails if release label present but no note?

anh: Yes, we can implement a `release-notes/required` check that triggers only for `release/*` labels. For `docs-only`, we allow a single sentence.

cameron: Rollbacks — if we roll back a release tag, what's the policy? Do we create `v1.4.2-rollback.1` or re-use tags?

mike: Do NOT re-use tags. Create `v1.4.3` as a rollback revert only if it's a forward-fix. For emergency revert, we should publish `v1.4.2-rc1`? That gets messy. I prefer: create `v1.4.2+revert.<date>` in annotated message and publish a new patch `v1.4.3` that reverts the bad changes.

jessica: TL;DR: never overwrite tags; prefer new patch that reverts. Annotated messages can carry `revert-of: v1.4.2`. Ops can pin older tag in deployment config if needed.

deploybot: NOTE: rollback playbook updated at https://go/release-playbook#rollback — recommends creating a revert commit and a new patch release.

anh: Sounds operationally safe. One more nuance: internal-only changes (infra, CI, docs in internal repo). Do we bump public package? I say no unless published artifact changes.

cameron: Agreed. If the published artifact (docker image, package) checksum changes, we must bump. Otherwise skip.

jessica: I'll draft a small RFC with: 1) `docs-only` label behavior, 2) tagging policy (`vX.Y.Z` refs + annotated build-meta), 3) release notes checklist, 4) rollback must create revert-pr + patch.

mike: Happy to review. Can we also add a small deploybot change to auto-suggest `docs-only` when PR touches only `docs/` or `website/`? That'd reduce mistakes.

anh: I'll file a follow-up ticket for deploybot heuristics and the PR template changes.

cameron: 👍 :shipit:
deploybot: ACTION: created issue #1428 `deploybot: auto-label docs-only for docs-only PRs` by anh."
